conclusion.text: The criterion treats a lower predicted BRENK alert count as preferable, using a deterministic RDKit-derived count of problematic substructures as a class-level heuristic for toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. It is a preference ordering, not a measured safety outcome, and the source claim does not report BRENK alerts or any toxicity data.

conditions.text: Applicability assumes a computable structure and the ADMET-AI BRENK_alert endpoint, with values sourced as database entries and determination treated as derived. The ordering is meaningful only if BRENK alerts track toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics in the relevant chemical space.

limitations.text: The source claim concerns combination therapy and drug-drug interaction risk, not BRENK alerts, so it does not validate the alert-to-safety link. No reference-set correlation, threshold, population, assay or units are provided, and the falsification test remains untested. Whether alert counts predict toxicity or pharmacokinetics for these compounds is unknown.

task_implication.text: For this oral multi-target agent task, the criterion offers a structural-liability signal that can be applied uniformly to every compound with a structure, complementing target-engagement evidence when comparing candidates. It does not itself establish CSF1R, VEGFR1-3 or FGFR1 activity, oral exposure, or clinical suitability.

context.conditions: assay: ADP-Glo kinase inhibition assay (Promega), 384-well, threefold dilution, triplicate; assay_protein_range_uM: 0.025; 0.2; buffer: 40 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5, 20 mM NaCl, 20 mM MgCl2, 1 mM TCEP, 0.1 mg/mL BSA, 4% DMSO; construct: FGFR1 kinase domain residues458-765; E.coli BL21 Rosetta expression; method_source_passages: locator_value: sec4.4.p1; quoted_span: The inhibition by sulfatinib was determined by the measurement of kinase activities following the ADP-Glo assay kit (Promega)6,44,45. Assays were performed in 384-well plates using sulfatinib (triple dilution method), proteins (0.025–0.2 μM), and poly (4:1 Glu, Tyr) peptides (Abcam, UK) (1 mg/mL) in assay buffer (40 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 20 mM NaCl, 20 mM MgCl2, 1 mM TCEP, 0.1 mg/mL BSA, and 4% DMSO). The reaction was initiated by the addition of ATP into the assay mixture, and then ADP-Glo was added to terminate the reaction and deplete the remaining ATP. Following the addition of detection reagent to convert the generated ADP to ATP, the luminescence was detected by a plate reader (Perkin Elmer). Samples were run in triplicate and the IC50 values were calculated by log[Inhibitor] versus kinase activity ratio in GraphPad Prism 8.0.; section_path: Methods; Kinase inhibition assay; locator_value: sec4.1.p1; quoted_span: FGFRs were prepared as previously described6,34,44,45. For crystallization, FGFR1C584S was co-expressed with untagged YOPH to induce non-phosphorylated proteins. The harvested cell pellets were lysed in a buffer containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 500 mM NaCl, 20 mM imidazole and 0.5 mM TCEP, and FGFRs were purified over Ni-NTA resin followed by enzymatic digestion with PreScission for 6×His-tag cleavage and further purified by anion exchange chromatography (GE Healthcare). For crystallization, FGFR1C584S was further purified by gel filtration chromatography (GE Healthcare). The proteins were concentrated to 5–16 mg/mL and stored at −80 °C.; section_path: Methods; Expression and purification of the human FGFR kinase domain; species: human; substrate: poly (4:1 Glu, Tyr), 1 mg/mL; target_variant: wild_type; unknown_conditions: ATP concentration; target-specific protein concentration; reaction incubation time
